title: When the Orbit Wakes Again
premise: Oscar Marchetti is the last active terraformer on Kepler Station Halcyon, tending a seed vault garden meant for colonists who will never arrive, while the colony's life support quietly fails and command stops answering. When they find an unfamiliar name—E. Voss—on the manifest of a ship that never launched, Oscar discovers a hidden program that recorded the memories of dying colonists into the station's relay, and that their own forgotten past is entangled with it. Racing a failing signal window to the edge-of-dead-space relay, Oscar must choose between broadcasting the colonists' stored memories (and their own buried guilt) to whoever might still be listening, or preserving the garden's power supply and letting the dead stay silent. In the end Oscar sends the signal, stays behind as the station's last witness, and plants the first seed in soil that finally breathes.
about_author: Wren Vane is the pen name of a former hydrology technician who spent six years at a remote research outpost before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep things alive when no one is watching.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Morning routine in the terraforming bay: checking humidity, pruning, logging data no one reads. We learn the colony is down to eleven people and command has gone silent for eight months. Emotional beat: tender devotion shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A census ping reveals the true population count; two names have vanished from the roster without death certificates. Oscar confronts engineer Priya Raghavan, who deflects. Beat: creeping unease beneath mundane maintenance.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Auditing old manifests in the archive, Oscar finds the freighter Meridian listed as crewed and launched—yet it sits gutted in Hangar 4, never flown. A name appears twice: E. Voss. Beat: the first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Priya's Warning
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She knows more than she says: the Meridian was refitted as an escape vessel, then scuttled by order of the last administrator. She warns Oscar to stop digging. Beat: fear disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: What the Soil Remembers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Tending the garden, Oscar finds root systems growing in patterns too regular to be natural—the vault is drawing power it shouldn't have. Something else is being fed. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Hangar 4
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Night break-in aboard the Meridian. Oscar finds a sealed memory core and a handwritten log signed E. Voss describing 'the recording'—colonists' minds archived before death. Beat: vertigo of touching the forbidden past.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Elena Voss's voice, years earlier: the decision to begin recording dying colonists' memories into the relay, framed as mercy. Beat: grief rationalized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Price of Eleven
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She confesses: the missing two colonists volunteered for early recording; the process killed them. Command didn't fail them—it harvested them. Beat: guilt shared like a wound.

chapters.title: Signal Window
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The edge-of-dead-space relay opens a transmission window in nineteen days—then closes for a decade. Whoever holds the memory core decides what humanity hears about Halcyon. Beat: stakes sharpened by the clock.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Technician Marcus Oyelaran's POV. Someone drains the garden's power reserve to charge the relay uplink. Oscar suspects Priya; Priya suspects the station itself. Beat: trust fracturing under scarcity.

chapters.title: The Fourth Voice
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The memory core activates near Oscar, playing a fragment: Voss speaking Oscar's childhood name. Oscar realizes they were one of the recorded—and their memories of Halcyon's founding are edited. Beat: identity collapse.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Extended flashback, Voss's POV: she chose Oscar—young, orphaned, idealistic—as the archive's living custodian, wiping the choice from their mind. Beat: love as manipulation, inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Vault
chapters.summary: Oscar and Priya's alternating POV. Priya admits she drained the power: she believes the dead should be sent, not the garden saved. They fight, then negotiate: enough power for either the seeds or the signal, not both. Beat: anger giving way to terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Preparations montage: jury-rigging the crawler, rationing oxygen, saying goodbye to the greenhouse rows. Marcus chooses to stay behind and keep the garden alive. Beat: quiet resolve.

chapters.title: Crossing the Gray
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, alone in the crawler across the dead surface. Dust storms, failing batteries, hallucinations of Voss's voice guiding and taunting them. Beat: endurance stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Arrival at the ancient relay; it's been maintained—recently. Footprints. Someone else has been waiting here. Beat: hope and paranoia arriving together.

chapters.title: The Listener
chapters.summary: New character Ilsa Reyes's POV: a scavenger-archivist who has kept the relay alive for years, waiting for exactly this transmission. She reveals other colonies died the same way—and someone is collecting their endings. Beat: the story widens beyond Halcyon.

chapters.title: Window Opening
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Six hours until the window closes. The core offers Oscar a choice encoded in Voss's final message: broadcast everything including Oscar's erased memories, or excise them and send only the others' voices. Beat: the thematic crux—survival versus truth.

chapters.title: What Oscar Sends
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, climax. Oscar transmits the complete archive—including their own shame about the harvest they unknowingly enabled—knowing it may brand them a collaborator forever. The signal goes out as the relay burns out. Beat: catharsis through self-exposure.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Ilsa and Oscar's POV. The relay is dead but the message is away. Ilsa offers passage on her ship; Oscar hesitates, looking back toward Halcyon's faint light. Beat: exhaustion, release, the ache of having told the truth.

chapters.title: Return to the Garden
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar returns to Halcyon—not to stay, but to bring Marcus and Priya seeds and news: a reply pulse, faint, from the inner colonies. Someone heard. Beat: cautious dawn after long night.

chapters.title: When the Orbit Wakes Again
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, coda. Months later: the station's orbit is corrected, the garden breathing, the first sprout breaking soil. Oscar records a new log—not for the dead, but for the living who are coming. Final beat: inheritance transformed from burden into gift.
